title: Perfect-complex duality on a small ringed site
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings and $D(\mathcal O)$ the unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $P\in D(\mathcal O)$ be perfect: locally on the site it is represented by a bounded cochain complex whose terms are direct summands of finite free $\mathcal O$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Use K-flat relative derived tensor [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then $P^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(P,\mathcal O)$ is perfect, the canonical bidual map $P\to(P^\vee)^\vee$ is an isomorphism, and for every $N\in D(\mathcal O)$ the canonical evaluation comparison is a natural isomorphism
$$P^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}N\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(P,N).$$

source.place: Tag 08JJ, label lemma-dual-perfect-complex; symmetry interchanges the tensor factors in the displayed isomorphism.

proof.text: Use the canonical maps $b_P$ and $e_{P,N}$ of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps]; the comparison in the statement is $e_{P,N}$ preceded by the symmetry $P^\vee\otimes^{\mathbf L}N\cong N\otimes^{\mathbf L}P^\vee$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], $P^\vee|_U=R\mathcal Hom(P|_U,\mathcal O_U)$, and the canonical maps restrict to the canonical maps of the slice site by [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps]. By the local perfectness condition of [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], every site object has a covering on each member of which $P$ is represented by a bounded complex $E$ of finite-free summands. Fix one such member and work on its localized ringed site; write its coefficient ring sheaf again as $\mathcal O$. Bounds and splitting ranks will be chosen only on this member.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, first paragraph; Tag 08JB, lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U

proof.text:
For any term $T=E^i$, choose its splitting $T\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal O^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{p}T$. With the standard sections $u_j$ and coordinate functionals $u_j^*$ put $t_j=p(u_j)$ and $\lambda_j=u_j^*i$, so $\sum_jt_j\lambda_j=1_T$. The sheaf Hom and tensor definitions [def-pur-sheaf-hom, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] give, for every module sheaf $B$, mutually inverse maps
$$B\otimes T^\vee\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom(T,B),\quad b\otimes\phi\longmapsto(t\mapsto b\phi(t)),\qquad h\longmapsto\sum_jh(t_j)\otimes\lambda_j.$$
Indeed their composites send $h$ to $h\sum_jt_j\lambda_j=h$ and $b\otimes\phi$ to $b\otimes\sum_j\phi(t_j)\lambda_j=b\otimes\phi$. All formulas are compatible with further restriction. The dual maps $p^\vee,i^\vee$ exhibit $T^\vee$ as a summand of $(\mathcal O^{\oplus r})^\vee=\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$. The double-dual map $t\mapsto(\phi\mapsto\phi(t))$ has inverse $\alpha\mapsto\sum_j\alpha(\lambda_j)t_j$. Finally $\mathcal Hom(T,-)$ is a retract, naturally in its argument, of $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal O^{\oplus r},-)=(-)^{\oplus r}$. The latter is exact by [lem-sc-finite-free-internal-hom-exact]. Applying the retraction to any short exact sequence splits its kernels, images and cokernels, so its retract sequence is exact too. Likewise $-\otimes T$ and $-\otimes T^\vee$ are retracts of the finite direct-sum functor and are exact; hence $T,T^\vee$ are flat by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

source.place: Tag 08JJ, final finite-free/direct-summand calculation; dual splittings and termwise evaluation

proof.text: Let $M$ be any complex on this slice, with no boundedness hypothesis. For the K-injective resolution $M\to I(M)$ used by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], the bounded-exact-source lemma [lem-pc-bounded-exact-term-hom-quasi-iso] and the exactness of every $\mathcal Hom(E^i,-)$ from step 2 show that $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,M)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,I(M))$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus the ordinary Hom complex canonically represents $R\mathcal Hom(QE,QM)$. By [def-pur-hom-complex] its degree $n$ term is $\bigoplus_i\mathcal Hom(E^i,M^{i+n})$: the product is a finite sum because only finitely many $E^i$ are nonzero. Its differential is $d_Mf-(-1)^nf d_E$. This comparison is the actual map induced by the resolution augmentation, so it is natural in $M$ and in chain maps of $E$.

source.place: Tag 08JH, lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect, ordinary-to-derived Hom comparison; bounded exact-source proof instead of its local-actual-map argument

proof.text:
Apply step 3 with $M=\mathcal O[0]$. Then $P^\vee$ on this slice is represented by $D=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\mathcal O[0])$, where
$$D^q=(E^{-q})^\vee,\qquad d_D^q=(-1)^{q+1}(d_E^{-q-1})^\vee.$$
The differential follows by substituting the zero differential of $\mathcal O[0]$ in [def-pur-hom-complex]. If $E$ is supported in $[a,b]$, then $D$ is supported in $[-b,-a]$. Step 2 gives finite-free-summand splittings for every $D^q$, so $D$ is strictly perfect. Applying the same argument to $D$ computes the derived double dual by its ordinary double Hom complex. This proves local perfectness of $P^\vee$, without imposing a global interval on $P$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, second paragraph, model of the dual and finite-free-summand dual terms

proof.text:
Under the two ordinary-Hom comparisons of steps 3 and 4, the canonical $b_P$ of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps] is the chain map
$$\beta^i:E^i\longrightarrow(E^i)^{\vee\vee},\qquad \beta^i(x)(\phi)=(-1)^i\phi(x).$$
The sign is the Koszul interchange of degrees $i$ and $-i$. To check the chain condition explicitly, [def-pur-hom-complex] gives the double-dual differential $d_{DD}^i=-(d_E^i)^{\vee\vee}$, and therefore $d_{DD}^i\beta^i(x)(\psi)=(-1)^{i+1}\psi(d_Ex)=\beta^{i+1}(d_Ex)(\psi)$. Each $\beta^i$ is invertible by step 2, with inverse $\alpha\mapsto(-1)^i\sum_j\alpha(\lambda_j)t_j$. Consequently the canonical bidual map is an isomorphism on this slice, including in odd degrees and in characteristic two. The two augmentation quasi-isomorphisms required by the normalization clause for $b$ in [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps] are those of step 3 (with $M=\mathcal O[0]$) and of step 4 (the same argument applied to $D$).

source.place: Tag 08JJ, second paragraph: canonical bidual map is termwise evaluation up to sign; Tag 0A97 for the canonical map

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $F\to M$ of the arbitrary restriction of $N$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By step 2, the terms of $D$ are flat; $D$ is bounded above by step 4. Thus [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes $D$ K-flat. Both $D$ and $F$ are therefore in the resolving class of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], so $N\otimes^{\mathbf L}P^\vee$ on this slice is represented by $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes D)$ with its canonical tensor comparison. Step 3 also identifies $R\mathcal Hom(P,N)$ with $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,F)$. None of these uses boundedness of $F$ or $N$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, final paragraph: choose a K-flat representative of M; Tags 06YS and 06YQ for K-flat resolutions and bounded-above flat complexes

proof.text:
In these models the canonical comparison $e_{P,N}$ of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps] has on the $(p,q)$ summand in degree $n=p+q$ the evaluation map
$$F^p\otimes(E^{-q})^\vee\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom(E^{-q},F^p),\qquad y\otimes\phi\longmapsto(x\mapsto y\phi(x)).$$
Its other Hom projections are zero. Step 2 proves each displayed map invertible for arbitrary $F^p$. For fixed $n$, the sum over $q$ is finite since $D$ is bounded; it is exactly the same finite indexing set on both sides. Thus the degree-$n$ comparison is an isomorphism. For the differential check, [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and step 4 give $d_Fy\otimes\phi+(-1)^{p+q+1}y\otimes(\phi d_E)$. Evaluation takes this to $d_Ff-(-1)^{p+q}fd_E$, precisely the differential of [def-pur-hom-complex]. This is the actual graded evaluation used in the canonical map, rather than an unspecified isomorphism between the objects. Preceding it by the Koszul symmetry $\phi\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes\phi$ gives exactly the comparison with the tensor order in the statement, also an isomorphism. This symmetry is its own inverse. For its chain condition, the coefficients of $d_Fy\otimes\phi$ and $y\otimes d_D\phi$ after either composite are respectively $(-1)^{pq}$ and $(-1)^{pq+p}$, directly from the tensor differential. The hypotheses of the normalization clause of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps] hold here: $F$ and $D$ are K-flat by step 6, and the two augmentation maps are quasi-isomorphisms by step 3 (with $M=\mathcal O[0]$ and $M=F$).

source.place: Tag 08JJ, last three displays and final sentence, including the evaluation map; section-hom-complexes for signs

proof.text: Local invertibility implies global invertibility. Restriction of module sheaves to slices is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], so it is computed termwise on complexes, sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, and commutes with kernels, images and hence cohomology; in particular the restriction of $Q(f)$ to a slice is $Q(f|_U)$. The small family of all slice objects chosen in step 1 covers the site in the sense of [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism]: for each object its chosen covering arrows already belong to that family's generated sieve. Let $\gamma$ be a morphism of $D(\mathcal O)$ whose restriction to every chosen slice is invertible. Choose K-injective representatives of its source and target by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] $\gamma=Q(f)$ for an actual chain map $f$. Each $H^n(f)|_U=H^n(f|_U)$ is invertible, since the cohomology functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] send isomorphisms to isomorphisms. The cited sheaf-cover criterion, applied to the morphism $H^n(f)$ of abelian sheaves, makes every $H^n(f)$ invertible. Thus $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $\gamma$ is invertible. By step 1 the restrictions of $b_P$ and $e_{P,N}$ to the chosen slices are the canonical maps there [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps], which are invertible by steps 5 and 7; hence $b_P$ and $e_{P,N}$ (and the comparison of the statement, which differs from $e_{P,N}$ by the symmetry isomorphism) are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, local-to-global passage; Tag 08FI, sites-cohomology-lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; Tag 070I, derived-lemma-K-injective, equivalence (1)/(3); Tag 079P, injectives-theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck.

proof.text: Perfectness of $P^\vee$. Take one global K-injective representative $J$ of $P^\vee$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. For each chosen slice $U$ its restriction $J|_U$ is K-injective by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized] and represents $P^\vee|_U$ by exactness of restriction. The local derived isomorphism $QD\cong P^\vee|_U=Q(J|_U)$ from step 4 is therefore $Q$ of an actual chain map $D\to J|_U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Its cohomology maps are isomorphisms ([def-weil-abstract-derived-category]), so it is a quasi-isomorphism. Since every object has such a covering (step 1) and each $D$ is bounded with terms direct summands of finite free $\mathcal O_U$-modules (step 4), the complex $J$ satisfies precisely the local condition of [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], so $P^\vee$ is perfect.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, local-to-global passage; Tag 08FI, sites-cohomology-lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; Tag 070I, derived-lemma-K-injective, equivalence (1)/(3); Tag 079P, injectives-theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck.

proof.text: Naturality. The maps $e_{P,N}$ are natural in $N$ by [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps], and so is the symmetry; since every component is invertible by step 8, composing each naturality square with the component inverses shows that the inverses are natural too, so the comparison is a natural isomorphism. Steps 8 and 9 together with this prove all three assertions.

Reused the existing ringed-site tools, created only the arbitrary-input canonical-map construction without any perfectness or invertibility conclusion. No statement or coefficient hypotheses changed. Second reading replaces the uncited roof argument with cited K-injective chain representatives, supplies actual local quasi-isomorphisms to one global representative for the literal perfectness definition, and checks the Koszul symmetry differential explicitly.
